entities.summary:
Smilis, the renowned ancient Greek sculptor, was born on the island of Aegina in 550 BCE. A contemporary of the legendary Daedalus, Smilis made significant contributions to the Aeginetan School of sculpture, which would later influence the development of Western art. As a painter and sculptor, Smilis was recognized for his exceptional skill and was associated with the archaic cult figure at the Heraion of Samos.


Smilis's father, Euclides, played a crucial role in shaping his son's artistic talents. The Aeginetan School of sculpture, under Smilis's leadership, produced renowned works that showcased the artist's mastery of form and technique. Smilis's legacy extends beyond his own time, as his works continue to inspire artists and art historians to this day.


The Heraion of Samos, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, remains a testament to Smilis's enduring impact on the world of art. As a cultural icon, Smilis continues to captivate audiences with his innovative and enduring artistic vision.
